newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel March CPI likely to depress shares-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Israel March CPI likely to depress shares-analysts.

text.p: Israel's higher than expected March inflation figure of 1.0 percent is likely to depress the Tel Aviv stock market on Wednesday, analysts said.

"Expectations were for a CPI of 0.7 to 0.9 percent. Some market players even expected a far lower CPI. The high figure is explained by the rise in the dollar which has caused a devaluation of the shekel," said Daniella Finn of Batucha Securities.
"I expect the market will react negatively in trading tomorrow," she said.
Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities called the figure very disappointing.
"It is clear that the Bank of Israel will not lower its key lending rate in the near future. It might even decide to raise the rates," Tsur said.
He said the stock market was expected to decline on Wednesday. The inflation figure was announced after the close of trading on Tuesday.
"In the short term the trend is expected to be negative because investors expected a rise of only 0.7 to 0.8 percent," Tsur said.
"The April CPI is also expected to be relatively high because of seasonal changes and the decline of the shekel against the dollar", he added.
